documentation.title: Free impact of two deformable disks
documentation.description:
A transient impact between two deformable bodies of CURVED geometry, with no applied load and nothing holding either body up. A contact patch forms, grows and releases.
Two disks of radius 0.05 m, 2e-4 m apart, butterfly-meshed so every element is a decent quadrilateral. The upper disk starts with a downward velocity, the lower one at rest and completely free.
NOTHING IS FIXED. That is the point, and it is what every other contact testcase gives up: a body held by a Dirichlet condition has its equilibrium supplied by the boundary, so the contact force is whatever balances a known load. Here the only force in the model is the contact traction. Expressing it needed an initial VELOCITY for a mechanic PDE, which was a schema gap rather than missing code -- note that quantity names the DERIVATIVE field (quantity="mechVelocity"), and that initialValues must come after contactList.
WHAT IT ASSERTS
1. contactForceX = 0. The model is symmetric about x = 0 in geometry, mesh and initial condition alike, so the contact traction can have no net horizontal component. Exact, independent of material, time step and mesh, and a real check: a mispaired point or a normal from the wrong facet breaks it immediately. 2. The contact state at the final step. Recorded, not predicted -- an impact has no closed-form contact force. What makes it worth asserting is that a free transient impact reaches a definite contact state at all. 3. That the run completes, which with no load and no support is not a formality.
The run stops mid-impact because that is where there is something to assert; after separation the contact state is all zeros. The patch is two points wide: the rim resolves the circle to 0.098 rad and the Hertzian patch is narrower than one facet, so this demonstrates a free impact between curved deformable bodies but does NOT resolve a Hertzian pressure distribution, and nothing here asserts one.
resStopCrit is deliberately loose and convergence is judged on incStopCrit: a free impact has no external load, so the residual has nothing to normalise against and falls back to an absolute value that is unreachable. normalSmoothing="nodal" because a butterfly-meshed rim is faceted and the patch sits right on top of the normal jumps.
